text:
marta: Filing a short postmortem for the prefetch livelock we saw during the tenant surge this morning (~09:12 UTC). Root cause hypothesis below, please react and add corrections.

liam: saw the alert, thanks. can you paste the key logs?

marta: pasted below — pattern is repeated prefetch -> demote -> immediate retry -> handoff -> demote again, looped until eviction credits exhausted and latency spiked.

marta: ```
[09:11:57] prefetch: tenant=acme id=42 attempt=1 prefetched=0 evict_hint=hot
[09:11:57] handoff: lease=lease_123 result=DENIED demote_count=1
[09:11:58] prefetch: tenant=acme id=42 attempt=2 prefetched=0 demote_reason=tombstone
[09:11:58] handoff: lease=lease_124 result=DENIED demote_count=2
[09:11:59] prefetch: tenant=acme id=42 attempt=3 prefetched=0 demote_reason=evict_score_high
[09:11:59] handoff: lease=lease_125 result=DENIED demote_count=3
[09:12:00] prefetch: tenant=acme id=42 attempt=4 prefetched=0 backoff=0s
... repeated until system tripped quota
```

ana: oka, so repeated immediate retries with backoff=0s. why is backoff 0? I thought we added jittered exponential backoff last quarter.

marta: agreed — looks like the prefetch admission code bypassed backoff when demote_reason in {tombstone, evict_score_high} to avoid undue wait for cold reads. that optimization didn't consider a degenerate multi-tenant surge where demote_count increments quickly.

tessa: and handoff was returning DENIED immediately which requeued prefetch attempts without increasing wait, right?

marta: right. Denied handoffs were translated to immediate retry in the prefetch loop instead of mapping to a backoff bucket.

liam: hypothesis: prefetch loop lacks a per-tenant retry cap and doesn't observe recent demote timestamps. combined with fast demote reactions (we demote on any tombstone/eject hint) you get rapid churn -> livelock and tail latency.

ana: minimal repro idea: simulate 50 tenants spamming hot prefix, ensure handoff denies occur, and see if prefetch retries multiply. I can spin that up in the perf lab.

marta: tests: please include demote_count and last_demote_ts in the metrics emitted by prefetch admission, and add a histogram of prefetch_retry_interval.

ops-bot: perf-lab job #542 queued (sim-id: prefetch-livelock-sim).

liam: proposed immediate fixes:
- map handoff DENIED -> increment tenant_prefetch_backoff counter and apply exponential backoff with capped jitter (min 10ms, max 2s)
- add a short-lived lease_bump token (100ms) to avoid immediate new handoff attempts after DENIED
- enforce per-tenant in-flight prefetch limit (default 2)

tessa: for longer-term:
- revisit "bypass backoff on tombstone" rule: change to "bypass only when tombstone && single-tenant low-load"
- prefetch admission should consult a small eviction-signal window (if demote_count > 2 within 1s, throttle prefills)
- add fairness token-bucket per-tenant for prefetch rate limiting

marta: implementation sketch (pseudo):
```go
// if handoff denied -> schedule retry with exp backoff
retry := tenantPrefetchRetry(tenantID)
retry.backoff = min(maxBackoff, base*2^retry.attempt)
retry.attempt++
retry.scheduled_at = now + jitter(retry.backoff)
```
Also on DENIED: bumpLease(tenantID, 100 * time.Millisecond) to reduce immediate contention.
```

ana: unit-tests we need:
- denied->backoff mapping preserves order and doesn't starve other tenants
- per-tenant in-flight limit enforced under concurrency
- eviction-bypass flag only skips backoff when global_load < threshold

liam: ops monitoring to add: prefetch_retry_count, prefetch_retry_interval_ms, prefetch_denied_rate, lease_bump_count, per_tenant_inflight_prefetch_gauge. add alert if prefetch_retry_count spikes 5x baseline and p95 latency > 200ms.

tessa: rollout plan: feature-flag the backoff mapping, enable for small subset (canary) first 10% of hosts, watch metrics for surge handling. If stable after 2 hours, widen to 100%.

marta: owner assignments:
- marta: implement denied->backoff mapping + lease_bump (PR next 48h)
- ana: perf-lab repro + tests (results EOD tomorrow)
- liam: metrics + alerts + dashboard panels
- tessa: rollout plan + feature flag gating

liam: small followup Q: do we want an absolute global prefetch cap to protect control-plane memory? might be useful as last resort.

marta: yes, add a global cap with soft-fail path that responds with 503 to callers (or falls back to direct readpath) and emits a strong alert.

ana: perf-lab job started. I'll post results in this thread.

ops-bot: deploy canary to hosts: canary-cc1 started (job #789).

marta: thanks everyone. I'll open the PR with the sketch and link here. we'll reconvene if perf-lab shows the same livelock after backoff changes. :thumbsup:
